Package gnu.x11

Class EscherSocket

java.lang.Object
gnu.x11.EscherSocket
public class EscherSocket extends Object
A socket to an X display.

For a local display (empty host, localhost, 127.0.0.1, or the running machine's own hostname) this class opens an AF_UNIX SocketChannel against /tmp/.X11-unix/X<n>. For a remote display it opens a TCP Socket against port 6000+n.

Why the rewrite: the original implementation had a JNI static initializer System.loadLibrary("Escher") and two native methods (socketCreateAndConnect(int), socketClose(int)) because JDK 15 and earlier had no first-class AF_UNIX socket support, so the local-display path had to be implemented in C. JDK 16 added UnixDomainSocketAddress plus StandardProtocolFamily.UNIX support in SocketChannel, which covers the same functionality in pure Java. As of the lg3d JDK-21 port this class no longer loads any native library, no longer holds a raw file descriptor, and no longer requires libEscher.so on java.library.path.

The EscherOutputStream and EscherDataInputStream adapters returned from this class are likewise pure-Java stream wrappers now that the fd-based constructors have been removed.

Abstract socket namespace: Xorg on Linux listens on the filesystem socket /tmp/.X11-unix/X<n> by default. Some hardened configurations also (or instead) expose an abstract-namespace socket @/tmp/.X11-unix/X<n>; UnixDomainSocketAddress in JDK 16+ does not support the abstract namespace, so if a target system uses only abstract sockets the caller must set FORCE_IP (via -Descher.forceIP=true) and ensure Xorg is not started with -nolisten tcp.
